reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer support for a first observation is retained because the final paper states that no coherent oscillations had been reported in 2D-material quantum devices and reports coherent charge oscillations in a BLG DQD (P:S-6d7d9008b84c3c6517d7; P:S-2f9698ca85cb93c1ffd0).

The residual novelty limit is independently supported by the final cross-platform comparison: PAT and Fourier-derived values are reported in the 400–500 ps range and compared with other material systems (P:S-7a41d2e80c2324dba6d5; P:S-f140c12701ccb98a4dff).

The final paper provides the retained experimental basis for the reported coherent oscillations: interference fringes are identified as the signature of coherent charge oscillations (P:S-75a7468e718175fdfbde), and the pulse-sequence mechanism is described in P:S-e2d47923b0ef442dae2d.

The retained cross-method strength is supported by the final PAT estimate and its 729-point distribution (P:S-f140c12701ccb98a4dff) and by the independently derived Fourier estimate (P:S-74331b1b8f9f5e6a27ec).

The final paper documents a calibrated PAT determination of the TLS dispersion and tunnel coupling (P:S-3231f82096aae31473fb; P:S-a3fcd7a553c478ce83d8), supporting the retained methodological strength.

The residual uncertainty remains explicit in the final paper: the PAT distribution has substantial variation attributed to frequency-dependent power transmission, and PAT power broadening makes the value a lower bound (P:S-f140c12701ccb98a4dff).
The final paper retains the first-fringe absence as a pulse-distortion effect and states that time-axis resolution is insufficient for quantitative decoherence analysis (P:S-fc7307581ce3a0e655e4).

The final paper reports PAT-derived tunnel couplings for three gate settings (P:S-a3fcd7a553c478ce83d8; P:S-43254ac0fb5b374aeaa1), while the directly presented coherent-oscillation analysis is performed in the selected intermediate-coupling regime; this leaves the coupling dependence of coherence only partially established in the final PaperIR.
The request for context on other 2D materials was resolved in the final paper, which discusses extensions to WSe2 and MoSe2 and material-dependent noise mechanisms (P:S-2f9698ca85cb93c1ffd0).

The question about spin and valley participation was resolved by final text specifying the applied field, valley polarization, and partial spin polarization in the PAT discussion (P:S-3231f82096aae31473fb).

The requests for pulse parameters, initialization, and current-readout details were resolved by final descriptions of the rate and initialization protocol (P:S-43254ac0fb5b374aeaa1; P:S-45fcc4a4250424aa268c) and DC measurement and calibration (P:S-cfc3cf63669292b45cd8).
The final PaperIR supplied in this package does not establish whether the requested second-device Figure R7 material was included in the Supplementary Information.

limiting_points.suggested_action: State the platform-specific scope alongside the comparison.
limiting_points.text: The novelty is platform-specific rather than a record-coherence claim: the 400–500 ps ensemble decoherence times are comparable to values in established semiconductor systems.

supporting_points.text: The specific contribution is the observation and analysis of phase-coherent charge oscillations in a bilayer-graphene double quantum dot, a platform where coherent oscillations had not previously been reported.

questions.suggested_action: Clarify the scope of direct coherence evidence across the reported coupling range.
questions.text: How do the coherent-oscillation signatures and their periods evolve across gate-tuned interdot couplings, beyond the intermediate-coupling regime used for the main interference analysis?

strengths.text: The interference-fringe measurements provide a concrete time-domain signature of coherent charge oscillations, with the LZSM pulse sequence and readout mechanism explicitly described.
Charge decoherence is estimated independently by PAT linewidths and Fourier analysis of LZSM data, yielding mutually consistent average values in the reported 400–500 ps range.
The PAT analysis quantitatively maps the two-level-system dispersion, extracts the lever arm and tunnel coupling, and is accompanied by pulse-amplitude calibration and measurement details.

summary.text: This study demonstrates coherent charge oscillations in a bilayer-graphene double quantum dot using LZSM interference and reports ensemble charge-decoherence times of roughly 400–500 ps from both PAT and Fourier analysis. Its contribution is the platform-specific observation of phase coherence, supported by complementary measurements, while the residual scope is set by PAT power/transmission variation, limited time-domain resolution, and incomplete direct mapping of coherence across tunnel-coupling regimes.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify the sensitivity of the PAT estimate to delivered microwave power.
weaknesses.text: The PAT-derived decoherence times show substantial variation associated with frequency-dependent transmitted power and power broadening; the paper therefore treats the PAT estimate as a lower bound.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Characterize pulse distortion at the first fringe and its impact on time-domain analysis.
weaknesses.text: Pulse distortion is invoked to explain the missing first-fringe oscillations, and the time-axis resolution is stated to be insufficient for a quantitative decoherence analysis in that domain.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Final discussion includes other 2D materials and material-dependent charge-noise considerations.
Final PAT discussion addresses the field-induced valley and spin splitting relevant to accessible excited states.
Final text specifies pulse rate, initialization logic, DC current readout, and calibration.
The supplied final PaperIR does not verify placement of the second-device Figure R7 material in the Supplementary Information.
